Aquatics
rows.notes: Living in/on water, in any form. From temporary pools to lakes and rivers.

rows.name: Indicators: Standing water
rows.notes: Primary habitat in/on pools, ponds, slow flowing water – including temporary ponds, but avoiding species specifically in vegetation and mud or banks of ponds.

rows.name: Indicators: Running water
rows.notes: Rivers and/or streams. Species predominantly found in these.

rows.name: Pasture/Dung
rows.notes: Grazed land of varying form. Includes most dung beetles, including those that are not stenotopic to dung. Mostly open landscape, but may include pasture-woodland when in combination with BEco4.

rows.name: Meadowland
rows.notes: Natural grassland or near equivalents. Open landscape.

rows.name: Wood and trees
rows.notes: Species tied to either the actual wood, trees or the forest/woodland environment. Generally shade tolerant.

rows.name: Indicators: Deciduous
rows.notes: Specifically deciduous wood or woodland, species not found on coniferous wood except on rare occasions.

rows.name: Indicators: Coniferous
rows.notes: Specifically coniferous wood or woodland, species not found on deciduous wood except on rare occasions.

rows.name: Wetlands/marshes
rows.notes: Water tolerant but not living specifically in the water. May include mud and bank species, as well as those moss & reed dwellers that prefer permanently wet environments.

rows.name: Open wet habitats
rows.notes: Hydrophilous shade intolerant species, shingle, beaches etc. and other exposed wet environments.

rows.name: Disturbed/arable
rows.notes: Any disturbed ground surface, be it by animal, geological or human action. Includes ploughed fields, edges of watering holes, farm yards, glacial margins etc.

rows.name: Sandy/dry disturbed/arable
rows.notes: Similar to the above, but more xerophilous species. Typifies beach, dune and aeolian landscapes, or ploughed fields on more sandy soils. A more dominant environment in southern Europe than BEco6a.

rows.name: Dung/foul habitats
rows.notes: A wide category for species that live in decaying, muddy and fetid environments, including compost, wet hay, dung and muddy edges of water.

rows.name: Carrion
rows.notes: Animal carcasses of all forms, dry or wet.

rows.name: Indicators: Dung
rows.notes: Primary habitat dung, or dung essential for reproduction. Includes parasites of other species that live in dung. Majority of species not found in other environments represented by the broader class BEco7a, but some may be found on occasions outside of dung.

rows.name: Mould beetles
rows.notes: Large part of the typical indoor synanthropic fauna in northern Europe.

rows.name: General synanthropic
rows.notes: In association with humans, either when outside of their ‘natural’ geographical range, or in all known records. This term may be geographically specific, and is used in a north European context here.

rows.name: Stored grain pest
rows.notes: Pests of stored products.

rows.name: Dry dead wood
rows.notes: Wood in constructions, but also similar natural environments such as large fallen trees, especially in warmer climates.

rows.name: Heathland & moorland
rows.notes: Heathland and moorland, but may also indicate the under-storey of a Boreal forest.

rows.name: Halotolerant
rows.notes: Salt tolerant, often coastal or salt marsh tied, but not just NaCl – can be species found on mineral rich ploughed soils or where mineral precipitation is prominent.

rows.name: Ectoparasite
rows.notes: External parasites of humans and animals
